stem: A 4-year-old child can self-report pain but cannot reliably use a numeric 0-to-10 scale. Which assessment tool is appropriate?

options.A: Require a numeric 0-to-10 rating because self-report is useful only when a child can assign a precise number to pain intensity.
options.B: Avoid self-report because young children cannot provide useful pain information even when they understand a developmentally appropriate tool.
options.C: Use a faces chart by comparing the child's observed facial expression with the pictured faces and assigning the matching score yourself.
options.D: Use the Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale if the child understands the instructions, asking the child to select the face that best represents the child's own pain.

rationale: The official Wong-Baker FACES Foundation states that the FACES Scale is used with people age 3 years and older and is a self-assessment tool. The patient must understand the instructions and personally select the face that best illustrates the physical pain being experienced; the scale should not be used by a parent, clinician, or other observer to match the patient's facial expression. Therefore D is correct for this 4-year-old who can self-report and understands the tool. A imposes a numeric scale the child cannot reliably use, B incorrectly excludes valid self-report, and C converts the FACES Scale into an observer-rated facial-expression tool.
educational_objective: Select and correctly use a developmentally appropriate self-report pain tool for a young child who understands the Wong-Baker FACES instructions.
source_document_title: Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale — Official Home and FAQs

source_claim_supported: The Wong-Baker FACES Scale is an age-3-and-older self-report tool for patients who understand the instructions; the patient selects the face, not an observer.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — developmentally appropriate assessment and interpretation of clinical findings.
correction_summary: Balanced alternatives around the same pain-assessment decision and preserved the critical distinction between patient self-report and observer facial-expression scoring.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — official Wong-Baker guidance directly supports age 3+, comprehension, and patient-selected self-report; C is specifically contraindicated use of the tool.
